## Summary

The May 1 and November 7, 2026 guides require a reader to be registered to a Location to accept payments. Registration requires a user role with write permissions. Smart readers have three registration methods. The listed mobile readers register while connecting via the SDK.

## Smart Reader Registration Methods

**1. Registration code (pairing code).** Obtain the code from the reader or regenerate it in admin settings. An unregistered reader shows the code when first unboxed. Use Dashboard or create a Reader through the API. The May Node and November cURL examples send `registration_code`, `label` and `location`. Use the code method to re-register a reader to another Stripe account.

**2. Serial number.** The Dashboard flow can register or re-register without physical access, up to **10 readers at a time**. Find the serial number in Hardware Orders, on the box or reader, or in the Reader details/API if already registered.

> **Serial registration scope (2026-05-01 and 2026-11-07).** May says the reader must have been ordered by the account and that either the platform or the sub-account must have placed the order to register it to a sub-account. November says serial registration cannot transfer a reader registered to an unrelated Stripe account. Under November’s Connect rules, a connected account that ordered directly and is outside the platform’s controls cannot have that reader registered to the platform account. For platform-placed orders, the connected account cannot self-register the reader. The platform registers on its behalf using the `Stripe-Account` header or **View Dashboard as**. The dated wording leaves the interaction with the broad May restriction unresolved.

**3. Order number.** Use this method for an order placed by the account or one of its connected accounts. In **Hardware Orders**, a `shipped` or `delivered` order’s **Register** action opens reader selection when serial numbers are assigned or the pre-registration flow when they are unassigned. The **Terminal Readers** registration flow also supports entering an order number and selecting registerable readers. A supplied name becomes a sequential prefix when registering multiple readers.

**Pre-registration (November).** Pre-select one Location per order. Stripe automatically registers the readers to it during fulfillment and serial assignment. Pre-registration stays within the same account, so a platform cannot pre-register the order to a connected account’s Location. To split an order among multiple Locations, use serial-number registration after assignment.

## Mobile Reader Registration

For Stripe Reader M2, BBPOS Chipper 2X BT and BBPOS WisePad 3, both guides document registration during the connection. The iOS and Android variants pass `locationId` in `BluetoothConnectionConfiguration`. React Native passes `locationId` in its `connectReader` call. Each variant can reuse the discovered reader’s `reader.locationId` for the last-used Location.

terminal-fleet-register-readers.Q1: At https://docs.stripe.com/terminal/fleet/register-readers, source-stripe-terminal-register-readers.md captures the baseline that payment acceptance requires registration to a Location and registration requires a write-permitted user. The smart-reader pairing code generated on the device is used in Dashboard or as registration_code when creating a Reader via API. Serial registration is remote and can batch up to ten. November routes unrelated-account transfers to the pairing code method and says that an order made by a connected account outside platform controls cannot register to the platform account. If the platform orders, it registers on the connected account's behalf with Stripe-Account or View Dashboard as, and the connected account cannot self-register that reader under this flow (old raw lines 8-46, old raw lines 48-70, new raw lines 9-48, new raw lines 50-66). Order-number registration requires an order from the account or an associated connected account. From a shipped or delivered order, assigned serials open selection and registration, while unassigned serials lead to pre-registration. Stripe registers to the chosen location during fulfillment and serial assignment. One location is allowed per order and cross-account pre-registration is excluded (old raw lines 72-98, new raw lines 68-102). For a mobile M2, Chipper 2X BT or WisePad 3 the app registers during connection, using locationId in BluetoothConnectionConfiguration for iOS/Android or directly in React Native connectReader. It can reuse the last location from the discovered reader's locationId (old raw line 104, old raw line 130, old raw line 162, new raw lines 106-110, new raw lines 134-138, new raw lines 168-180). The original summary omitted the November Connect and pre-registration conditions and generalized the native configuration path. The revision makes the three methods and their actor and SDK scopes explicit.
terminal-fleet-register-readers.Q2: At https://docs.stripe.com/terminal/fleet/register-readers, source-stripe-terminal-register-readers.md preserves both full captures and the November pre-registration and delegation conditions. The May 1 guide gives a broad serial order ownership qualifier. The November 7 guide explicitly distinguishes unrelated-account transfers, connected-account direct orders outside platform controls, and platform-placed orders requiring platform action to register on behalf of the connected account. This is a documentation expansion, without evidence of when the product rules first took effect or that broader eligibility has been relaxed (old raw lines 48-60, new raw lines 39-48). Preserve the order-number order provenance and distinguish the new Hardware Orders serial-assignment branch: automatic fulfillment-time registration after pre-selecting one location, no across-account pre-registration, and serial-number registration after assignment when splitting the order among locations (old raw lines 72-98, new raw lines 68-102). Heading/numbering, the Locations link, Node.js-to-cURL pairing example and Swift/TSX edits are presentation or navigation, with mobile variants already differing in argument placement (old raw lines 26-46, old raw lines 102-126, old raw lines 160-179, new raw lines 19-37, new raw lines 106-132, new raw lines 168-189). The proposed reciprocal hardware-orders route dates its serial restriction and corrects the mobile SDK phrasing. The Terminal concept route retains connect-time registration and links the Source guidance that distinguishes the SDK variants and requires a Location.
